editorial:
You know that feeling when your phone buzzes and you can't help but check it? Selfie takes that everyday struggle and cranks it up to eleven. The film follows several people whose lives fall apart because of their obsession with screens, apps, and social media. From a family dinner ruined by phones to a workplace meltdown over a viral video, each story shows how technology turns ordinary moments into total chaos. The tone is loud, silly, and relatable, with characters who feel like people you know. It's an anthology, so you jump between stories, but they all connect through one big idea: we are all a little too attached to our devices.

The acting is energetic and over the top in the best way, with performers who commit to the madness. The pacing keeps things moving fast, though some stories land better than others. A few jokes feel repetitive, and the humor can be a bit much if you are not in the mood. Still, if you enjoy light, chaotic comedies about modern life, this one is a fun ride.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, each storyline crashes into one another at a big family gathering where everyone is glued to their phones. The twist comes when the one character who refused technology all along turns out to be secretly running a viral account. Realizing the irony, the group finally puts their devices away and actually talks to each other. The movie ends on a hopeful note, suggesting that while technology is here to stay, real connection still matters most.
